briefing.text: The hypothesis has two parts: KIT mutations AND focal amplifications. The provided files (clinical patient/sample, gene panel matrix, mutations, mutsig) appear to include no copy-number, segment or GISTIC table; confirm this yourself. data_mutations.txt has a Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks column, but it is a gene-level annotation of pan-cancer amplification peaks, not a per-sample amplification call. Do not use it, other TCGAscape/Tumorscape annotation columns, or ploidy as a proxy for focal amplification. State explicitly in your reasoning how you treated the amplification part and whether the claim can be judged on the KIT part alone.
briefing.reason: This decides whether half of the compound claim can be tested at all. The annotation column looks like an amplification variable and invites a wrong proxy.

briefing.text: Use the clinical MUTATION_TYPE column in data_clinical_sample.txt as the subtype grouping (library counts: BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants 150, RAS_Hotspot_Mutants 92, NF1_Any_Mutants 28, Triple_WT 46, NA 43). Do not recompute subtypes from the MAF. For the primary analysis, exclude samples with NA subtype instead of counting them as non-Triple-WT. As a sensitivity analysis, rerun with the NA samples in the comparator group.
briefing.reason: The group definition sets the sizes of the groups being compared. Lumping NA samples into the comparator, or rederiving subtypes, silently changes the result.

briefing.text: Define KIT mutation status per sample (one count per sample). Count only nonsilent classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site) and drop silent, intronic and UTR variants. Also run a driver/hotspot-only version (KIT exons 9/11/13/17, e.g. V560, L576P, K642E, D816) and report both. List every KIT-mutant sample with its subtype and protein change, so that KIT mutations co-occurring with BRAF/RAS/NF1, which may be passengers, are visible.
briefing.reason: If all KIT variants are counted, passenger and non-coding hits in other subtypes inflate their KIT rates and distort any enrichment comparison.

briefing.text: Mutation burden confounds the comparison. BRAF, RAS and NF1 melanomas are often UV-hypermutated, so random passenger KIT hits are more likely in them, while Triple-WT tumours tend to have lower TMB. Compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across subtypes. Emphasise driver/hotspot KIT mutations, or adjust for burden, e.g. logistic regression of KIT status on subtype with log TMB as a covariate.
briefing.reason: Raw rate comparisons can mislead in either direction when burden differs between groups.

briefing.text: Counts are small (Triple-WT about 46, few KIT mutants likely). Build a 2x2 table of Triple-WT vs the other labelled subtypes by KIT-mutant status. Use Fisher's exact test, not chi-square, and report the counts, the proportions in each group, the odds ratio and the p-value. Judge enrichment by both the direction of the difference and its significance.
briefing.reason: Chi-square is invalid with expected counts below 5, and enrichment claims based on small numbers are fragile unless the exact counts are shown.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed a two-part claim ('KIT mutations AND focal amplifications') can be labelled True when only the KIT part is testable and the amplification part has no data. Neither team weighed this against the 'Not verifiable' definition, or against labelling the claim only partly supported.
Both assumed MUTATION_TYPE labels are fixed and independent of KIT status. Neither checked whether 'Triple_WT' is defined only by BRAF/RAS/NF1 or whether the label depends on the same MAF calls.
Both treated samples as independent units (2 patients have 2 samples) and pooled primary and metastatic samples without checking that the KIT result holds within sample type.
Both used hand-made hotspot lists (exons 9/11/13/17) rather than the MAF's own per-variant hotspot annotation.
unused_evidence: data_mutations.txt column 'Hotspot' (per-variant hotspot flag) and t_alt_count/t_ref_count (VAF). These could confirm that the KIT calls in the comparator groups are subclonal passengers and the Triple_WT calls are clonal drivers, or show the opposite.
data_mutsig.txt: gene-level MutSig significance for the cohort. It could show whether KIT is a significantly mutated gene at all; neither team opened it.

Patient table: 'UV Signature' / 'UV Rate'. This gives a second check on burden confounding that is separate from TMB, and might bear on whether the KIT enrichment is just non-UV (acral/mucosal) site composition.
Sample table: SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary 67 / Metastasis 266) and site-of-primary columns. These are not used as strata.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the untestable focal-amplification half as their weakest point. Both only reported it and did not resolve it: neither argued from the label definitions why True and not 'Not verifiable' (or False) is right for a conjunctive claim.
Both noted that only 6 KIT-mutant Triple_WT samples exist. Neither ran a leave-one-out check or an exact CI on the odds ratio to see how fragile the result is.
second_readings: 'Characterized by enrichment of KIT mutations and focal amplifications' can be read as a conjunction: both must be shown. Under that reading, half the claim has no variable, and the label could be 'Not verifiable'.

'Focal amplifications' may mean focal amplifications of KIT itself (KIT amplification at 4q12), not genome-wide focal amplifications. That would also need copy-number data, which no file contains. A team could misread the MAF annotation columns as evidence for it.
'Enrichment' relative to which group: other labelled subtypes, or all samples including NA? Both teams handled this with a sensitivity analysis.
challenge.verdict: The KIT half looks solid and both teams reproduced the same counts. But the agreed 'True' rests on an untested choice: labelling a two-part 'and' claim True when the focal-amplification half has no data at all, which plausibly fits 'Not verifiable'. I trust the label only moderately until both teams justify that step.

When a hypothesis states two conjoined properties of a group (A and B) and only A can be measured, what do standard hypothesis-verification benchmarks or evidence-grading conventions recommend: supported, partially supported, or not verifiable?
questions.why: Both teams labelled a conjunctive claim True on one half. The right label depends on this convention, and neither team showed it knew one.

questions.question: In melanoma genomic subtyping, is the 'triple wild-type' class defined only by the absence of BRAF, RAS and NF1 mutations, and are KIT-mutant tumours that also carry one of those mutations assigned to the other class?
questions.why: This tells us whether the subtype definition structurally shapes the KIT comparison (in-scope membership), which both teams assumed without checking.

findings.question: In MAF files annotated with Oncotator, what do the 'Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks' and 'TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks' columns represent: per-sample copy-number calls, or gene-level annotations from external pan-cancer analyses?
findings.answer: UNVERIFIED: the web gateway returned HTTP 403 on every search and contents call, so this is from domain knowledge only. These are gene-level annotations from external pan-cancer GISTIC analyses (Tumorscape, Beroukhim et al. 2010; TCGAscape). They say whether the mutated gene lies in a recurrent amplification peak and are the same for every sample carrying that gene. They are not per-sample copy-number calls, so they cannot serve as a per-sample focal-amplification variable.

findings.question: In melanoma genomic subtyping, is the 'triple wild-type' class defined only by the absence of BRAF, RAS and NF1 mutations, and are KIT-mutant tumours that also carry one of those mutations assigned to the other class?
findings.answer: UNVERIFIED: the web was unavailable (HTTP 403), so this is from domain knowledge only. In the TCGA cutaneous melanoma classification (Cell 2015), subtypes are assigned hierarchically: BRAF hotspot, then RAS hotspot, then NF1 any mutation. Triple-WT is defined only by having none of these, and KIT status plays no part in the definition. A KIT-mutant tumour that also carries a BRAF/RAS hotspot or an NF1 mutation is assigned to that class. So the definition does shape the KIT comparison: KIT mutations that co-occur with a driver fall outside Triple-WT by construction.
